title: Effects of road traffic noise on sleep: Studies on children and adults

limitations: No knowledge/control of individual noise exposure levels (indoors with closed and open windows) for every single bedroom.
Uncertainties in traffic load distribution for day and night in highest noise category, potentially overestimating Lnight.
Possible noise-insulating measures taken by house-owners in the highest noise exposure category without informing local authorities, leading to lower indoor noise levels than predicted.
Wrist-actigraphy comparisons between different studies and age groups should be done with greatest care due to differences in actigraph types and body motility with age.
Poor correlation between sleep logs and actigraphy for number and duration of awakenings, as self-report is subjective and actigraphy may misinterpret stillness as sleep or restless sleep as wake.
